correctness.rationale: The finite-tree incidence map is an isomorphism modulo constants; the exact edge matrix block decomposition and two-eigenvalue kernel give the central row. Other edge rows are strictly dominated because the rational Laplace transform of q+dk-exp(-t) factorizes into four positive scalar resolvents. Strict positivity and the central extremizing gradient prove every-time sharpness; two exponential rates establish the unique peak and its asymptotic. Independently replayed 63 matrix tests match to 4.619e-14, supplementary only. No unproved infinite extrapolation is required.

value.rationale: The all-time sharp norm with edge location and one attaining function determines a canonical graph heat stability invariant and equivalent optimal adjacent-pair W1 mixing separation. The diameter-three bottleneck produces a nontrivial amplification limit 3, qualitatively beyond the star/bipartite 2-scale. The sharp 8/d finite-size deficit and unique transient peak have a natural operator/transport interpretation and are not just renamed spectral eigenvalues.
